title: Sebastian and the Provision
premise: Paloma Lockridge, a desert ranger who has spent nine years outrunning a warrant for a fire she didn't set, is hired to track a thief who stole provisions from an upriver expedition camp. Following the trail, she finds the expedition slaughtered or scattered by the mining syndicate whose illegal dig they uncovered, with only the expedition's teenage cartographer, Sebastian, still alive and carrying evidence that could ruin the syndicate. Pursued by syndicate enforcers and the monsoon itself, Paloma must choose between her invisibility and getting Sebastian home to testify. She delivers him to the district court just as the monsoon breaks, sacrificing her anonymity to do so, and finds that the found family she built along the river is willing to shelter her when the law finally catches up.
about_author: Coral Delacroix is the pen name of a former river-guide and search-and-rescue volunteer who spent a decade in the badlands of the American Southwest. She writes adventure stories about people who keep moving, and about the families they build when they finally stop.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Left a Trail
chapters.summary: Paloma, first-person POV, is hired by the expedition's outfitter to track the provision thief. She reads the desert like a ledger and expects an easy payday, but the thief's trail is deliberate, almost communicative. Emotional beat: her practiced solitude cracking with curiosity as the trail refuses to behave like a thief's.

chapters.title: Nothing on the Radio
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Reaching the upriver camp, she finds it burned, supplies looted, and the expedition's satellite radio smashed. The thief's trail converges here, then splits toward the gorge. Emotional beat: dread displacing professionalism; the realization that she was hired to find a symptom, not a cause.

chapters.title: Sebastian
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She corners the thief in a slot canyon and discovers Sebastian, the expedition's sixteen-year-old cartographer, who stole provisions to survive after witnessing the syndicate's massacre of his team. Emotional beat: two fugitives recognizing each other's fear; the first fragile trust.

chapters.title: What the Map Showed
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He shows Paloma his maps, which document the syndicate's illegal dig and the mass grave beside it. He insists the evidence must reach the district court before the monsoon seals the river. Emotional beat: his guilt at surviving, and Paloma's terror at becoming a witness instead of a ghost.

chapters.title: The Syndicate's Men
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Enforcers sweep the gorge, forcing the pair into the flooded caves. Paloma uses ranger tricks to misdirect them, but realizes the syndicate knows a ranger is helping the boy. Emotional beat: her old instinct to vanish warring with her new refusal to leave Sebastian behind.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Landing
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. They reach the isolated river settlement of Ferrymen's Landing, where Paloma's past resurfaces: the ferryman, Odile, once testified against her. Instead of betrayal, Odile hides them, feeds them, and offers boats. Emotional beat: the first taste of found family, and Paloma's disbelief at being sheltered anyway.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The monsoon arrives early; the river rises, and the syndicate's boats close in. A running gunfight through the rapids costs them their supplies, and Paloma takes a bullet graze. Emotional beat: desperation sharpening into resolve; she stops calculating escape and starts calculating victory.

chapters.title: The Turnaround
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Trapped on a mesa, Sebastian turns the tables by broadcasting the syndicate's crimes over the salvaged radio to every ranger station in the district, making the pair too famous to kill quietly. Emotional beat: the quiet boy claiming his voice, and Paloma realizing the evidence is safer in the open than in hiding.

chapters.title: The Last Ford
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The climax: a final chase through the rising flood to the district courthouse, enforcers behind and the river rising. Paloma, wounded, carries Sebastian the last stretch and walks into the courtroom soaked and bleeding, surrendering her anonymity to put the evidence on record. Emotional beat: sacrifice as liberation.

chapters.title: What Stays
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, weeks later. The syndicate's leaders are indicted; Paloma's old warrant is dismissed when Odile and the Landing community testify for her. Sebastian, apprenticed to the district survey office, asks her to stay. Emotional beat: belonging chosen at last; the woman who kept moving finally has a reason to stop.
